body.statement:
For every \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in
\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), the explicit cross-fitted saturated-cell
one-step estimator in \(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) satisfies
\[
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 =\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)
   +o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
\[
 \frac{\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}}{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}
 \longrightarrow1
 \quad\text{in }Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\text{-probability},
 \qquad
 \frac{\sqrt n\{\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)\}}
      {\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1).
\]
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathbf P=(P_n)\in
\mathcal B_{\epsilon,M,c_0,v_0,v_1}\), and suppress the row subscript on
\(p_k,\pi_k,\mu_{ak}\).  All constants below may depend on
\(\epsilon,c_0,K_0\), but not on \(n,d_n\), or the chosen member of the
triangular class.  By \(def:balanced\text{-}local\text{-}class\), the row
law satisfies \(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\), \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\),
\(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\),
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\),
\(ass:balanced\text{-}cell\text{-}masses\),
\(ass:local\text{-}dimension\), and
\(ass:efficient\text{-}variance\text{-}band\).  In particular,
all probability-order notation below is under \(Q_{P_n}^{(n)}\), and
\[
 v_0M^2\le V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\le v_1M^2.
\tag{1}
\]

First derive the nuisance rates.  For a validation fold \(I_s\), let
\(m_s=n-|I_s|\) be its training size.  Since \(K_0\) is fixed and fold sizes
differ by at most one, \(m_s\ge c_Kn\) for a constant \(c_K>0\) and all
sufficiently large \(n\).  Let \(N_{ak,-s}\) and \(N_{k,-s}\) be the
corresponding training arm-cell and cell counts.  Cauchy--Schwarz and
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\) give
\[
 E_{P_n}[(Y-\mu_{ak})^2\mid X=k,A=a]
 \le
 \{E_{P_n}[(Y-\mu_{ak})^4\mid X=k,A=a]\}^{1/2}
 \le M^2.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(N\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(m,q)\), integration of its probability
generating function yields
\[
 E[(N+1)^{-1}]=\int_0^1(1-q+qt)^m\,dt
 =\frac{1-(1-q)^{m+1}}{(m+1)q},
 \qquad
 N^{-1}\mathbf1\{N>0\}\le2(N+1)^{-1}.
\tag{3}
\]
Conditionally on \(N_{ak,-s}=r>0\), the fitted cell mean is the average of
\(r\) observations from the conditional arm-cell law, so (2) bounds its
conditional mean-squared error by \(M^2/r\).  When \(r=0\), the zero fallback
in \(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\) has squared error at most \(M^2\)
by \(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\).  With
\(q_{ak}=P_n(X=k,A=a)\ge\epsilon p_k\), equations (2)--(3), the lower mass
bound \(p_k\ge c_0/d_n\), and \(\sum_kp_k=1\) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E\!\left[\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
  (\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak})^2\right]
 &\le M^2\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 \left\{e^{-m_sq_{ak}}+\frac{2}{(m_s+1)q_{ak}}\right\}\\
 &\le C_{\epsilon,c_0}M^2
 \left\{e^{-c_{\epsilon,c_0}m_s/d_n}+\frac{d_n}{m_s}\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
For the propensity estimate, condition on \(N_{k,-s}\).  On a nonempty cell
the empirical treatment proportion has conditional variance at most
\(1/(4N_{k,-s})\); on an empty cell its squared error is at most one.
Projection on \([\epsilon/2,1-\epsilon/2]\) cannot increase distance from
\(\pi_k\in[\epsilon,1-\epsilon]\).  Repeating (3) gives
\[
 E\!\left[\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
  (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)^2\right]
 \le C_{c_0}\left\{e^{-c_{c_0}m_s/d_n}+\frac{d_n}{m_s}\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Assumption \(ass:local\text{-}dimension\) implies
\(n/d_n\gg\sqrt n\), so the exponential terms in (4)--(5) are negligible
relative to \(d_n/n\).  Markov's inequality applied to (4)--(5), for each of
the fixed number of folds, yields
\[
 \|\widehat\mu_a^{(-s)}-\mu_a\|_{P_n,2}
   =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M\sqrt{d_n/n}),
 \qquad
 \|\widehat\pi^{(-s)}-\pi\|_{P_n,2}
   =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(\sqrt{d_n/n}).
\tag{6}
\]

Define the uncentered augmented score
\[
 g(O;\eta)=m_1(X)-m_0(X)
 +\frac{A\{Y-m_1(X)\}}{e(X)}
 -\frac{(1-A)\{Y-m_0(X)\}}{1-e(X)},
\tag{7}
\]
where \(\eta=(e,m_0,m_1)\), and let
\(\eta_0=(\pi,\mu_0,\mu_1)\).  Conditional-mean definitions,
\(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\), and \(def:ate\text{-}functional\) give
\[
 E_{P_n}[g(O;\eta_0)]=\tau(P_n),
 \qquad g(O;\eta_0)-\tau(P_n)=\phi_{P_n}(O)
\tag{8}
\]
by \(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\).  For the nuisance
estimate trained outside fold \(s\), put
\(D_s(O)=g(O;\widehat\eta^{(-s)})-g(O;\eta_0)\).  Conditioning on the
training sample and evaluating (7) cell by cell gives the exact identity
\[
 P_nD_s=\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)
 \left\{
 \frac{\widehat\mu_{1k}^{(-s)}-\mu_{1k}}
      {\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 +\frac{\widehat\mu_{0k}^{(-s)}-\mu_{0k}}
      {1-\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}}
 \right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
Every denominator in (9) is at least \(\epsilon/2\).  Cauchy--Schwarz and
(6) therefore show
\[
 |P_nD_s|=O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(Md_n/n)
          =o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}),
\tag{10}
\]
where the last step uses \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) and the fixed scale \(M\).

The same score algebra, \(|\widehat\pi-\pi|\le1\), the clipped denominators,
and (2) imply
\[
 P_nD_s^2\le C_\epsilon\left[
 \sum_{a=0}^1\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\mu_{ak}^{(-s)}-\mu_{ak})^2
 +M^2\sum_{k=1}^{d_n}p_k
 (\widehat\pi_k^{(-s)}-\pi_k)^2\right]
 =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M^2d_n/n).
\tag{11}
\]
By \(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\), the validation observations in \(I_s\) are
independent of \(\widehat\eta^{(-s)}\).  Conditional Chebyshev inequality and
(11) give
\[
 (\mathbb P_{I_s}-P_n)D_s
 =O_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(M\sqrt{d_n}/n).
\tag{12}
\]
Summing (9)--(12) over the fixed folds, with weights \(|I_s|/n\), and using
\(def:saturated\text{-}one\text{-}step\), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widehat\tau^{\mathrm{OS}}-\tau(P_n)
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{g(O_i;\eta_0)-\tau(P_n)\}
   +O_P(Md_n/n)+O_P(M\sqrt{d_n}/n)\\
 &=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)
   +o_{Q_{P_n}^{(n)}}(n^{-1/2}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
\]

For the variance, \(ass:cell\text{-}mean\text{-}envelope\) and
\(def:ate\text{-}functional\) give \(|\tau(P_n)|\le2M\).
Using \(ass:fixed\text{-}overlap\),
\(ass:conditional\text{-}fourth\text{-}moment\), and
\(|x_1+x_2+x_3|^4\le27\sum_{j=1}^3|x_j|^4\) in
\(def:efficient\text{-}influence\text{-}function\) yields
\[
 E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}(O)|^4\le C_\epsilon M^4.
\tag{14}
\]
Consequently Chebyshev's inequality, (1), and (14) give
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)^2
   -V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)=o_P(M^2),
 \qquad
 \overline\phi_n^2=o_P(M^2).
\tag{15}
\]
Conditioning fold by fold in (11) and applying Markov's inequality gives
\[
 \frac1n\sum_{s=0}^{K_0-1}\sum_{i\in I_s}D_s(O_i)^2
 =O_P(M^2d_n/n)=o_P(M^2).
\tag{16}
\]
For real arrays \((u_i)\) and \((v_i)\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \left|\frac1n\sum_i(u_i+v_i-\overline u-\overline v)^2
       -\frac1n\sum_i(u_i-\overline u)^2\right|
 \le2\left\{\frac1n\sum_i(u_i-\overline u)^2
             \frac1n\sum_i(v_i-\overline v)^2\right\}^{1/2}
      +\frac1n\sum_i(v_i-\overline v)^2.
\tag{17}
\]
Writing, for \(i\in I_s\),
\(\widehat\psi_i=\tau(P_n)+\phi_{P_n}(O_i)+D_s(O_i)\), and applying (17)
with \(u_i=\phi_{P_n}(O_i)\), \(v_i=D_s(O_i)\), equations (15)--(16) prove
\[
 \widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)=o_P(M^2).
\tag{18}
\]
Division is legitimate by the lower bound in (1), which proves
\(\widehat V^{\mathrm{OS}}/V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)\to1\).

Finally, (1) and (14) imply
\[
 \sup_n\frac{E_{P_n}|\phi_{P_n}(O)|^4}
                 {V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)^2}
 \le C_\epsilon/v_0^2<\infty.
\tag{19}
\]
The mean-zero identity needed by
\(lem:order\text{-}one\text{-}self\text{-}normalized\text{-}clt\) is (8);
\(ass:iid\text{-}sampling\) and (1) supply iid sampling and positive
variance.  That established lemma and (19) give
\[
 \frac{\sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)}
 {\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n[\phi_{P_n}(O_i)-\overline\phi_n]^2\right\}^{1/2}}
 \Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{20}
\]
Equation (15) makes the denominator in (20), divided by
\(\sqrt{nV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}\), converge in probability to one.  To avoid
invoking any undeclared limit theorem, fix \(x\in\mathbb R\) and
\(0<\delta<1\), and intersect with the event that this ratio lies in
\([1-\delta,1+\delta]\).  According to the sign of \(x\), the distribution
function of the oracle standardized mean is then bounded above and below by
the distribution functions in (20) evaluated at the smaller and larger of
\(x/(1-\delta)\) and \(x/(1+\delta)\), plus the probability of the complement
event.  First letting \(n\to\infty\), then \(\delta\downarrow0\), and using
continuity of the standard-normal distribution function gives
\[
 \frac{1}{\sqrt{nV_{\mathrm{eff}}(P_n)}}
 \sum_{i=1}^n\phi_{P_n}(O_i)\Rightarrow N(0,1).
\tag{21}
\]
Combining (13), (21), and the lower variance bound in (1) proves the asserted
normal limit.  This establishes every claim of the benchmark theorem without
using either heavy-light radius.
body.justification: This is the fully proved local Gaussian benchmark required by the directive and is not presented as the globally honest heavy-light result.
body.gap: Its weighted nuisance rates, orthogonal expansion, variance ratio, and central limit theorem are derived on the declared balanced triangular class.
body.consumer: It formalizes the efficient saturated-cell comparator for regular versions of the 401(k) table.
